t: 50 Field Notes for AI/ML Engineers
k: Fifty concentrated, opinionated lessons from building machine learning systems that run in production — each one a claim and the reason it is true.

t: Data
Modelling
LLM application work
Evaluation
Production
Working
Look at your data. Actually look at it.
Your label is the product, and it is probably wrong.
Point-in-time correctness is not a detail.
Missing is a value, not an absence.
Normalise before you deduplicate.
If your data pipeline is not idempotent, it is not finished.
Always build the stupid baseline.
On tabular data, beat gradient boosting before reaching for a network.
Overfit one batch before you train on everything.
Check that the initial loss is what theory says.
Learning rate is the hyperparameter that matters. Tune it first, tune it properly.
Ranking well and being calibrated are different skills.
Complexity must earn its place with a measurement.
Read the failures. Fifty of them, categorised.
Prompts are production code.
Fine-tuning teaches form. Retrieval supplies facts.
Constrain the output rather than asking politely.
Tell the model what to do when it does not know.
Retrieved text is data, never instructions.
Five good chunks beat thirty mediocre ones.
Log the transformed query, not just the original.
Agents compound errors multiplicatively.
Temperature zero is not deterministic in a batched server.
A large share of 'the model is stupid' reports are tokenisation.
Build the evaluation set before the feature.
Measure retrieval and generation separately.
Programmatic checks before model-based ones.
An uncalibrated judge is a random number generator with good manners.
Include the questions your system should refuse.
A flaky quality gate gets disabled within two weeks.
Benchmark scores are not production evidence.
Check segments, not just the average.
ML systems fail silently and stay up.
Training-serving skew is the most common production defect.
Shadow deployment is the most valuable step teams skip.
A rollback procedure nobody has executed is a hypothesis.
Deletion has to reach the caches too.
Denominate cost by successful outcome, not by request.
Idle accelerators are the most wasteful line in most ML budgets.
Instrument freshness as a number.
One request id should reconstruct everything.
Automatic retraining without an evaluation gate is automatic deployment of a worse model.
Iteration speed is the real constraint on model quality.
Reproduce something in your first two weeks on a new team.
Read the incident history before the architecture docs.
Kill your own project when it deserves it.
Describe what the model does mechanically, never what it 'understands'.
Report your own regressions before anyone else notices.
Fundamentals compound; releases do not.
Propose the cheap decisive experiment instead of winning the argument.
